title: How Many ATP Are Produced in Glycolysis? Test Yourself
description: Walk the four steps that spend or make ATP, then take a six question self-test on net versus gross, per glucose versus per pyruvate, and no oxygen.
intro: Six questions on the parts of this tally that cost people marks, all answerable from the table above.

questions.q: What does one glucose net from glycolysis?
options: 2 ATP, 2 NADH, 2 pyruvate
4 ATP, 2 NADH, 2 pyruvate
2 ATP, 4 NADH, 1 pyruvate
4 ATP, 4 NADH, 2 pyruvate
questions.why: Four ATP are made but two were already spent, so the net gain is 2 ATP alongside 2 NADH and 2 pyruvate.
questions.source: Answer box at the top: Net 2 ATP, four made and two spent, plus 2 NADH and 2 pyruvate.

questions.q: Phosphoglycerate kinase is listed as +2 ATP at step 7. Why is it not +1?
options: Pyruvate kinase later reverses one of the two ATP
Aldolase split the sugar, so the step runs twice
The enzyme phosphorylates ADP at two active sites
One ATP comes from step 7 and one from step 10
questions.why: The step makes 1 ATP per three-carbon molecule, and glucose was already split into two of them at step 4, so it is +2 per glucose and +1 per pyruvate.
questions.source: Note under the step table: steps 7 and 10 show +2 because aldolase splits the six-carbon sugar at step 4, so everything after that happens twice per glucose.

questions.q: Which two steps of glycolysis consume ATP?
options: Steps 7 and 10, phosphoglycerate kinase and pyruvate kinase
Steps 1 and 7, hexokinase and phosphoglycerate kinase
Steps 1 and 3, hexokinase and phosphofructokinase-1
Steps 3 and 10, phosphofructokinase-1 and pyruvate kinase
questions.why: The investment phase spends ATP at steps 1 and 3, while steps 7 and 10 are the payoff steps that make it.
questions.source: Step table rows 1 and 3: hexokinase -1 ATP, phosphofructokinase-1 -1 ATP.

questions.q: With no oxygen present, what does glycolysis net per glucose?
options: 0 ATP, the pathway stalls at step 6 instead
1 ATP, because pyruvate kinase cannot run
4 ATP, since no NADH gets cashed in later
2 ATP, the same as it nets with oxygen
questions.why: Glycolysis never uses oxygen, so the net stays 2 ATP and what changes is only the downstream fate of the pyruvate and NADH.
questions.source: Answer box and the section With oxygen versus without: glycolysis nets the same 2 ATP either way.

questions.q: How is ATP actually made during glycolysis?
options: A phosphate is handed from an intermediate to ADP
ATP synthase is turned by the proton gradient
Electrons travel down the chain and reduce oxygen
NADH is oxidized by complex I and the energy stored
questions.why: This is substrate-level phosphorylation, a direct transfer onto ADP, which is why no gradient, chain or oxygen is involved.
questions.source: Section How that ATP is actually made: a phosphate is handed directly from a high-energy intermediate onto ADP, at steps 7 and 10.

questions.q: What do the 2 ATP spent in the investment phase accomplish?
options: They reduce NAD+ so the payoff phase keeps running
They pay to carry glucose across the membrane inward
They are handed back to pyruvate kinase at step 10
They add phosphate and trap the sugar inside
questions.why: Phosphorylating the sugar puts a charge on it so it cannot cross back out of the cell, which is what the spent ATP buys.
questions.source: Section Why the net is 2 and not 4: hexokinase attaches a phosphate which traps glucose inside the cell because the charged molecule cannot cross the membrane back out.
